PACK BRIEFING — AMERICAS: A historic California bill that provides a refundable employment tax credit for qualifying local news organizations could soon become law, pending Gov.

Why it matters: Local news advocates believe the first-of-its kind measure, if signed into law, would represent the country's largest single-state investment in community news ever.

"This bill is the big one," said Steven Waldman, founder and president of the Rebuild Local News coalition, which sponsored the bill.

"It's where we have planted the flag as the ideal." Zoom in: The measure — which passed California's Senate on Sunday and Assembly on Monday — gives refundable tax credits to qualifying local newsrooms for employing full- and part-time journalists.

The credit is worth $20,000 for up to five full-time positions and $15,000 for every full-time journalist beyond that.

Part-time journalists are supported with a $7,500 credit.

There's also a $15,000 credit for new hires, incentivizing newsrooms to expand.

Context: Because the tax credit is open-ended, many newsrooms qualify.

https://www.axios.com/2026/09/01/california-local-news-tax-credit-bill

Scoreboard update: An expected drop in the unemployment rate has failed to materialise, dealing a setback to Andy Burnham’s hopes of reviving Britain’s ailing economy.

Unemployment remained stuck at 4.9pc in the three months to June, while the number of payrolled employees fell by 13,000, according to figures from the Office for National Statistics.

Economists had predicted that the unemployment rate would ease to 4.8pc.

Unemployment jumped to 5.4pc in June, up from 4.6pc the previous month.

Meanwhile, vacancies dropped to 707,000 in the three months to July – the lowest level since 2021 – with a particular strain on entry-level job openings.
